levels.0: Says 'run cron jobs' with no job definition, retry, overlap or visibility requirements.
levels.1: Covers one-off and cron jobs with retries, but leaves out time zones, overlap policy, cancellation or run history and logs.
levels.2: Defines a job (image, schedule with time zone, timeout, retry and overlap policy), runs as the unit of execution, pause/edit/manual run/cancel, per-run status and logs, and puts DAGs explicitly out of scope.

levels.0: No targets, or promises exactly-once execution.
levels.1: States the 5 s start target and at-least-once, but not that a skipped or lost run must be visible, or that the hour mark is the design point.
levels.2: Start within 5 s at p99, no silent loss (executed or visibly skipped/dead), duplicates rare and visible, firing more available than the owner API, and the hour-mark and midnight peaks named as the design point.

levels.0: Only the daily average, or numbers with no derivation.
levels.1: Computes about 116 runs/s and notes a peak, but never quantifies runs due in one second or the fire rate needed.
levels.2: 10M ÷ 86,400 = 115.7/s; 1.2M hour-aligned ÷ 24 = 50,000 due at once → 10,000 fires/s for the 5 s target, 20,000/s at midnight; concludes the average sizes nothing.

levels.0: No estimate of running jobs or worker capacity.
levels.1: Estimates concurrent runs but not heartbeat and claim load on the run store, or the worker slots needed.
levels.2: Little's law: 115.7 × 120 s = 13,889 running, about 63,900 after an hour mark and 113,900 at midnight; claims + heartbeats ≈ 14,400/s and about 28,000/s; 32 slots per host → about 600 hosts normally, 2,000 and 3,600 pre-warmed.

levels.0: A 'create job' endpoint with no shapes, and no worker protocol.
levels.1: Job CRUD and run status with bodies, but no idempotency, no starting deadline, or no fencing in the worker calls.
levels.2: POST /v1/jobs with Idempotency-Key, cron + time zone, retry, overlap and starting deadline; run IDs derived from job + scheduled time; manual run, pause, cancel, paged history; claim/heartbeat/complete carrying the attempt number and returning 409 when the lease is lost.

levels.0: One table of jobs polled by everything.
levels.1: Separates jobs from runs but has no index for 'what is due', or no conditional writes for claims.
levels.2: Postgres jobs with (partition, next_fire_at) index and per-partition epoch and fired_through; runs in a KV store keyed by job + scheduled time with conditional writes and TTL; leases in etcd; history in a search index; logs in object storage.

levels.0: A box diagram with a 'scheduler' and 'workers' and no flow.
levels.1: Walks create and fire, but claim, heartbeat, retry and the reaper are vague.
levels.2: Walks create, look-ahead, fire (enqueue only), claim with conditional write, heartbeat and log streaming, reaper and retry, and owner reads, over a multi-AZ layout sized from the estimates.

levels.0: Scans every job every second, or relies on one cron daemon.
levels.1: Uses a next-run index but fires only when due, with no look-ahead, or ignores time zones and daylight saving.
levels.2: Indexed next_fire_at in UTC, 60 s look-ahead into an in-memory timing wheel or heap, Postgres writes spread before the hour, and an explicit daylight-saving policy for skipped and repeated hours.

criteria.title: Leader election vs partitions, and no double firing

levels.0: Several schedulers with no coordination, or one leader with no failover story.
levels.1: Leases or leader election, but no fencing, so a paused scheduler can act after losing ownership.
levels.2: Compares one leader with partitioned leases and chooses by failover blast radius and throughput; epoch fencing on writes; idempotent run ID so duplicate fires are harmless; takeover re-fires from a watermark rather than assuming.

levels.0: Claims exactly-once, or has no way to detect a dead worker.
levels.1: Uses a visibility timeout or heartbeats, but zombie workers can still report results, or owners get no guidance on idempotency.
levels.2: Explains why exactly-once is impossible; queue visibility until claim, then run-row lease with heartbeats; attempt number as fencing token; scheduled time and run ID passed to jobs; maxAttempts 1 for non-idempotent jobs with a LOST alert.

criteria.title: Retries, overlap and the hour-mark herd

levels.0: Immediate unlimited retries; no plan for 50,000 simultaneous runs.
levels.1: Backoff and a dead state, but no jitter or overlap policy, or the herd handled only by 'autoscale'.
levels.2: Exponential backoff with full jitter, permanent exit codes, DEAD state, retries below on-time runs; allow/forbid/replace overlap; pre-materialise, pre-warm from the known schedule, H-style spreading; a zone-loss timeline at midnight.

criteria.title: Run visibility and detecting a late scheduler

levels.0: Owners check logs on the worker; no platform health signal beyond CPU.
levels.1: Run history and failure alerts, but nothing detects a scheduler that silently stopped.
levels.2: Timestamped run states and chunked logs, absence alerts per job, schedule-lag SLO, expected-vs-fired auditor per partition, and an external dead man's switch fed by canary jobs.

levels.1: Covers instance loss and names generic trade-offs, but not etcd quorum loss, a silent stop, or what breaks first at 10×.
levels.2: Covers scheduler death and pauses, etcd and Postgres failure, worker death, retry storms and silent stops; at 10× names worker cost first and mandatory spreading; each key decision is paired with its alternative and the reason it lost.
